text:
maya: Heads up — hitting consistent chart jank on console main in eu-canary since the telemetry-client v2 rollout at 08:12. Charts freeze for ~600-900ms when interactions start, even on cached queries. :eyes:
liam: saw that too in prod telemetry — is this the same client that switched to batched events + prefix KV header?
sarah: yes, v2 enabled prefix-KV hints and switched prefetch priority. Metrics show individual tile fetches are fine, but the main thread stays busy parsing more telemetry envelopes.
juan: adding logs — in the client we see a flurry of small parse operations: `parseTelemetryEnvelope` called 120x in 30s for one dashboard. That feels like a hot path.
alex: can you paste the flamegraph link?
maya: https://internal.traces/redwood/fg/1711005555 — it's dominated by `telemetryClient.processBatch` and then our chart render `computeLayout`. The interesting bit is the order: telemetry parse -> render -> render blocked waiting on JS parsing.
liam: suspecting two vectors: 1) telemetry client now does sync JSON.parse for some envelopes and 2) bundle change moved a big helper into the main chunk so parse cost is on main thread.
sarah: confirmed the helper (fast-decode) ended up in main chunk after new splitpoint changes. Before it lived in a worker polyfill we lazily loaded.
maya: quick experiment idea: toggle telemetry batching to async parse (set deferParse=true) and revert the helper import location. Can we try toggling in canary via feature flag?
juan: I pushed a hot flip to canary flag `telemetry.defer_parse` — deploy-bot reports rollout started: deploy-bot: "canary feature toggle telemetry.defer_parse=true at 1711005580"
maya: testing on eu-canary now — local nav + drag shows immediate improvement, freeze drops to ~80-120ms. :thumbsup:
liam: nice. But that only masks the root cause. We should also consider routing/quota interactions: our prefetch router currently routes telemetry to the same routes that drive kvcache evictions with the new quota buckets. If quotas cause repeated fetches, we get repeated parse cycles.
sarah: added a quick grep of routing policy changes last week — config diff: `routing.policy.prefetch = "affinity_v2"` and `quota.bucket.size = 150` — lowering bucket size increases eviction frequency.
(quoted config)
```
# changeset 2026-03-20
routing:
  policy: affinity_v2
quota:
  bucket:
    size: 150  # previously 300
```

alex: so smaller bucket -> more frequent prefetch miss -> more telemetry envelopes -> more parses. Combo land.
maya: proposal: 1) revert bucket size to 300 for eu-canary for 24h, 2) land async parse in telemetry-client, 3) plan a small bundle split so fast-decode moves into a worker-shared chunk.
juan: can we do 1) now? I can flip the quota config to 300 in canary and monitor.
liam: also we should add a microbenchmark for telemetry parse cost into our perf suite so future rollouts catch this.
sarah: created a perf test PR: `eng-platform/telemetry-parse-bench` — runs on CI and reports parse latency per envelope.
maya: for rollout UX, let's add a canary alert that watches main-thread parse time > 200ms per second over 60s and auto-pause telemetry batching. That way we don't degrade charts for users.
alex: agree. I'll draft a runbook for rollback steps: revert quota, flip defer_parse, emergency split request to eng-runtime.
juan: flipped bucket to 300 at 1711005603 — deploy-bot: "quota.bucket.size set to 300 in eu-canary (change 2026-03-20 17:00UTC)"
maya: after the quota flip plus defer_parse=true, interaction traces look back to normal on eu-canary. Leaving the flag on for additional monitoring.
liam: follow-ups: - schedule bundle split ticket - add telemetry parse bench to the release gates - instrument kvcache-miss -> telemetry-envelope rate in console metrics
sarah: noted. I'll open tickets and tag owners.
maya: thanks all — huge help triaging. We'll reconvene if anything spikes back up. :rocket:
